fix_subject: hotfix: stop prompting agent/reviewer to wrap installs in sfw (#1625)
intro_subject: feat: prompt open-swe to use socket firewall (#1576)
what_broke: Prompt told the agent to prefix package installs with the sfw (Socket Firewall) wrapper; those installs hung inside the sandbox.
evidence_quote: Installs hung when prefixed with sfw inside the sandbox (trace 019f0608 stalled on a pending `sfw npm install` execute, never returned).
replay_notes: Hard: needs the sandbox image with sfw (added by e599166e5/c3292d825); task = any repo needing npm install; compare prompt at 0f842e26a^ vs 0f842e26a.

fix_subject: fix: include resolved repo in Linear prompt to prevent repo ambiguity (#1307)
intro_subject: feat: stop auto-cloning and let agent manage repo setup [closes OPE-21] (#1159)
what_broke: A squash-merge dropped the line that told the LLM which repo a Linear task resolved to, so the agent guessed and silently targeted the wrong repository.
evidence_quote: This is a regression: commit 5e4c6bb8 ... added this exact line, but it was dropped when that branch was squash-merged as PR #1159
replay_notes: Moderate: feed a Linear-style task without repo in prompt and check which repo the agent clones; prompt-assembly difference is visible by diffing process_linear_issue at 2039fe666^ vs 2039fe666.

fix_subject: fix: stop task context from posing as the latest turn (#3795)
intro_subject: feat: task coordinator and asynchronous workers (#3658)
what_broke: TaskCoordinationMiddleware appended its task <dynamic-context> as the last message on every model call, so after each tool result the model saw it as a fresh event and a coordinator looped on slack_no_reply_needed (note: this fix was itself reverted the same day by 4dd5899da, reason not stated).
evidence_quote: A Slack coordinator waiting on a worker then called `slack_no_reply_needed` 279 times in one run, about every 5 seconds with roughly 120k tokens of context each time.
replay_notes: Moderate: needs the middleware plus a coordinator thread waiting on a worker; check number of repeated no-reply tool calls with context last vs first.

fix_subject: Revert "feat: add minimal diff rules and scope planning to agent prompt (#1171)" (#1174)
intro_subject: feat: add minimal diff rules and scope planning to agent prompt (#1171)
what_broke: Prompt section of hard 'Minimal Diffs' rules and a plan-your-file-list step was reverted the same day it merged (reason not stated in message).
evidence_quote: Revert "feat: add minimal diff rules and scope planning to agent prompt (#1171)"
replay_notes: Easy to diff (single prompt file, 14 lines) but the evidence of worse behaviour is not stated; any coding task in a repo would exercise it.

intro_subject: feat: add repository skill support to the coding agent (#1774)

fix_subject: fix: prevent futile retry loop when commit_and_open_pr fails (#1210)
what_broke: When git checkout or the PR API failed, the tool returned a generic failure with no no-retry signal, so the agent looped until the recursion limit.
evidence_quote: causing the agent to loop 9-13+ times until hitting the 1000-step recursion limit
replay_notes: Moderate: needs a failing git checkout/PR creation to trigger; introducing commit not identified (tool error shape probably original).

fix_subject: fix(open-swe): hotfix — reviewer fetches its own diff via gh (#1261)
intro_subject: feat: add reviewer graph + eval target wiring (#1241)
what_broke: Host-side diff prep (clone + git diff in sandbox) produced empty diffs for some PRs, so the reviewer agent silently published a 'no issues found' review.
evidence_quote: The host-side prep ... was producing empty diffs for some PRs. The agent then silently published a "no issues found" review
replay_notes: Moderate: needs a PR to review; intro pinned by date proximity (reviewer graph added the day before, 8d52e1761 fixed diff-prep error swallowing), not by blame.

intro_subject: feat: authenticate git operations via sandbox proxy instead of credential files [closes: OPE-20] (#1070)

fix_subject: fix(mda): honor explicit model switches on the next call (#4153)
what_broke: The performance-switch tool saved the requested model and reported success, but MDA's next-call selection ignored it and kept the cached main model.
evidence_quote: saved the requested model and confirmed success, but MDA's next-call selection ignored `requested_model` and `requested_effort`
replay_notes: Hard: MDA runtime; introducing commit not identified.

fix_subject: fix(middleware): reduce concurrent subagent state updates (#3077)
what_broke: Forked general-purpose subagents returning the same middleware state keys in one superstep made LangGraph reject the concurrent update and abort the parent run.
evidence_quote: LangGraph rejects those concurrent updates even when the values match and aborts the parent run.
replay_notes: Moderate: fan-out of forked subagents is enough; introducing commit not identified.

fix_subject: fix: reviewer publishes against stale head_sha on mid-run re-review (#1393)
what_broke: A push landing mid-run was queued into a run whose frozen config held the old head_sha, so review was anchored to the stale commit and last_reviewed_sha regressed.
evidence_quote: publish_review then anchored the GitHub review to the stale commit and regressed last_reviewed_sha to it
replay_notes: Hard: needs a PR push during an active reviewer run; introducing commit not identified.

fix_subject: fix(langgraph,prebuilt): give Send-dispatched tool calls the same state as an edge (#9728)
intro_subject: fix(prebuilt): hydrate ToolNode state from channels via pregel helpers (#7594)
what_broke: ToolNode hydrated state from raw channel values for bare tool-call lists, so on Pydantic/dataclass state graphs ToolRuntime.state and InjectedState got plain dicts instead of the state model.
evidence_quote: tools get the state as a plain dict of channel values ... The same tools reached through an edge ... get the model.
replay_notes: Easy: small StateGraph with Pydantic state, a tool using InjectedState, tool calls dispatched via Send('tools',[tool_call]); run at f4aee546^ vs f4aee546 (needs the paired langchain create_agent change for realistic path).

fix_subject: fix(langgraph,prebuilt): stop ToolNode from swallowing invalid resume values (#9232)
what_broke: A pydantic ValidationError from interrupt(response_schema) raised inside a tool was treated by ToolNode as bad model arguments and fed back to the model, hiding the error from the human.
evidence_quote: the human never sees the error, the model is blamed for it
replay_notes: Easy once identified, but the intro is the original ToolNode error handler, not a discrete regression commit.

fix_subject: fix(prebuilt): make wrap_tool_call state overrides reach the tool (#9730)
what_broke: ToolCallRequest.override(state=...) did not change what tools saw, because injection read state from request.runtime which the override left unchanged.
evidence_quote: `ToolCallRequest.override(state=...)` is a documented override, but tools never saw the new state.
replay_notes: Easy: wrap_tool_call that overrides state plus a tool with InjectedState; likely related to 7045a231 (added state override, 2026-01-09) but not verified.

fix_subject: fix: AttributeError: type object 'datetime.datetime' has no attribute 'datetime' (#178)
intro_subject: Fix: Resolve strftime ValueError on Windows (#126)
what_broke: A Windows strftime fix called datetime.datetime.now() while the module imported the class, so get_today_str raised AttributeError in normal runs.
evidence_quote: AttributeError: type object 'datetime.datetime' has no attribute 'datetime'
replay_notes: Easy: call get_today_str (used in every prompt) at 0c9b239; deterministic crash, no LLM needed.
